morphemes.form: -rq (-yrq after f or b; also written as a separate word 'rq')
morphemes.function: Copula / predicate marker 'is'. It closes a verbless nominal clause; gy-rq and gt-rq mean 'this is (X)'.
morphemes.evidence: It ends every clause of the descriptive formulas. After the 3,465 words ending in -rq, the next word is typically a clause opener: a title (rykeqbp 441, xaqotb 400, xbtgq 178, ukfy 157), NAME (334) or the offering noun xby (114); 256 of them end the text. It is written as a separate word 313 times (stbkjtfy rq 86, njqbt fy rq 43, btaqntfy rq 4), so it is a clitic. It attaches with or without the determiner, so it is a separate morpheme: kfy-rq 42 vs kfy-fy-rq 17, sqayptbt-rq 21 vs sqayptbt-fy-rq 13, gy-rq 149, gt-rq 71. A linking vowel letter (y, sometimes t) appears after consonantal f and b: -f-y-rq, -b-y-rq, -ot-bt-rq.

morphemes.function: Determiner / definite article on common nouns. The vowel letter after f depends on what follows: -fy before the copula or at clause end, -fq inside a noun phrase (possessors, appositions, before genitive -w), -ft before plural -o.
morphemes.evidence: Proper names do not take it (2 of 1,999 NAME tokens: one in the T0019 list where f follows every item, one in the fragment 'NAME fy kwgtby'), but common nouns in the same possessor slot do: 'xaqotb NAME stbkjtfyrq' vs 'xaqotb bhybtmbtfq stbkjtfyrq' and 'xaqotb btjtgtfq oft stbkjtfyrq'. It is written apart in 'NAME ktbt f' (115 times 'ktbt f'). It is optional on predicates (kfy-rq vs kfy-fy-rq). The same stems show the shapes side by side: btjvt-fq / btjvt-fy-rq, btaqnt-fq / btaqnt-fy-rq, nayay-fq / nayay-fy-rq / nayay-fto, ubt-fq / ubt-fy-rq, bkmbt-fy-rq / bkmbt-fto / bkmbt-fqw, wk-ft / wk-fy-rq. Some labels end in -fy with no copula (htfkyu X ebnt fy; ... btnt fy). 42 word types end in -fyrq, 62 in -fq, 31 in -fto.

morphemes.function: Determiner + copula: turns a relational noun into the clause predicate, '(the deceased) is the X of [the preceding person or title]'.
morphemes.evidence: 2,309 tokens on 42 word types. It always follows a possessor (NAME, title + NAME, or a noun in -fq / -fto) and ends the clause: NAME btjvtfyrq (65 times), NAME btaqntfyrq (90), NAME stbkjtfyrq (447), NAME wkfyrq, NAME ubtfyrq, NAME kyntfyrq. Split spellings show its parts: stbkjtfy rq (86), btaqntfy rq (4), njqbt fy rq (43).

morphemes.function: The determiner in non-final position: marks a common noun that is a possessor, an apposition or a list item inside the noun phrase, not the predicate.
morphemes.evidence: In the possessor slot before the relational noun: bhybtmbt-fq stbkjtfyrq, btjtgt-fq oft stbkjtfyrq, pfpq-fq btbtfqbatfq stbkjtfyrq, bagfp-fq stbkjtfyrq, kbt-fq stbkjtfyrq, xua-fq kavt-fq sqrf rq. As an apposition before the predicate form of the same noun: 'NAME btjvtfq btjvtfyrq' (34) and 'NAME btaqntfq btaqntfyrq' (13). In labels: X uktjtfq (21), rbtfq hntfq (21). Before the genitive: -fqw (19 types).

morphemes.function: Plural marker. It appears in the plural determiner -ft-o, the genitive plural -bt-o, the plural copula -ft-o-nrq and the plural-possessor element -(gt)-o-t- in predicates.
morphemes.evidence: Words with -fto / -bto are list items or possessors that a plural predicate refers back to: 'htfkyu fto xhybt fto vahv fto njqbt otw fy'; 'htfkyu xbyfqbto fpraywbtfto fpkyjfqbto vahvm ugtnqbtfto njqbtotbyrqe'. -ftonrq appears only in T0892, the one text that names two people ('gy kypq gyrq xoaqbt hktbt gyrq'), on the terms that are -fyrq in single-person texts (stjvt-ftonrq, btaqnt-ftonrq, staqbt-ftonrq).

morphemes.function: Plural (collective) determiner, the plural of -f-: 'the X-s', mostly on possessors.
morphemes.evidence: 31 word types, 180 tokens. It fills the possessor slot that -fq fills elsewhere: bkmbt-fto stbkjtfyrq (13 texts) beside bkmbt-fyrq and bkmbt-fqw; bbm-fto, ujywbt-fto, htjtktbt-fto, bntbyatbt-fto, xbqstbt-fto, uyuymbt-fto + stbkjtfyrq. Plural predicates follow -fto possessors: 'xeb key bkmbtfto njqbtgtotbyrq', 'rnqbt bkmbtfto ubtxgtotbyrq', 'kw uqatkaynt nayayfto ubtotbyrq'. It is written apart in lists: 'htfkyu fto xhybt fto vahv fto'.

morphemes.function: Plural predicate: plural determiner -fto + a copula with -n- ('they are the X of'), used when the subject is more than one person.
morphemes.evidence: Only 3 tokens, all in T0892, which nominates two people ('gy kypq gyrq xoaqbt hktbt gyrq'). There the filiation and relation terms end in -ftonrq (stjvt-ftonrq, btaqnt-ftonrq, staqbt-ftonrq) where single-person texts have -fyrq (btaqnt-fyrq in 195 texts).

morphemes.function: Plural possessor ('of these / of them') inside the predicate: '(is) a relative of these'. gt is the deictic (as in gt ... gtrq) and o the plural marker.
morphemes.evidence: Every attestation follows a list or a plural possessor. F1 ends 'xbtgq NAME hga NAME otfyfynt NAME otfyfynt NAME otfyfynt NAME xbtgq NAME stbkjt xgtotbyrq' (86 texts). F3: 'kftntsyw batst ... kftntsyw bnatst ntfr stbkjtotbyrq' (21). F4: 'katogy nbbatfto katogy gyaybto ntfr stbkjt xgtotbyrq' (13), 'bkmbtfto njqbtgtotbyrq' and 'bkmbtfto ubtxgtotbyrq' (13). Labels: 'htwby X htwby e stbkjt otbtrq' (21, two htwby), 'hga NAME NAME stbkjt gtotw fyrq'. Single possessors get plain -fyrq. Written alone it takes the initial x (xgtotbyrq 99); attached it does not (stbkjtgtotbyrq 4, njqbtgtotbyrq 13).

morphemes.function: Genitive / linker 'of': ties a title or noun to what follows ('the htaqbt of the xjo, NAME'). Before the determiner f it fuses into b (w + f > b).
morphemes.evidence: The same frames are spelled both ways: 'b jvt RNAME gyat w f NAME' (8) = 'bjvt RNAME gyatb X' (21); 'htaqbt ryu w fto' (4) = 'htaqbt ryubto' (2); 'htfkyu xby fq w fto fp rayw bt fto fp kyj fq w fto' (T0562) = 'htfkyu xbyfqbto fpraywbtfto fpkyjfqbto' (T0010). As -fqw (19 types, written 'fq w' 43 times) it closes a title phrase before a name: 'htaqbt xjofqw NAME' (13 texts), 'htfkyu xjofqw X' (21), 'xkyfp puvwfqw NAME', 'uuqktbt nbntfqw NAME'; compare 'hyfkyu w NAME' or 'hyfkyu w st' (21) beside 'hyfkyu NAME' (14).

morphemes.form: -b- (= fused w + f; in -byrq, -bto, gyatb, ryuby)
morphemes.function: Fused genitive + determiner 'of the'. It gives a second predicate ending -b-y-rq ('is the X of the ...') and the plural possessive -bt-o.
morphemes.evidence: The fusion is shown by the spelling pairs under -w. -byrq stands where other nouns have -fyrq: kjt-byrq (86 texts, 'gyat wkft NAME kjtbyrq'), njq-byrq (21), vuvw-fq-byrq (39 tokens), kfq-byrq (13), xaykt-fq-byrq, kptsy-byrq, enjtsy-byrq, kftsy-byrq. -by alone: 'htaqbt ryuby' (21) = 'htaqbt ryu w f(to)'.

morphemes.function: Vocative (address) ending on the two invoked divine names and their epithets; -sq after a stem ending in t.
morphemes.evidence: ryu-q is text-initial in 158 of its 178 uses and otherwise mostly recurs right after the last offering wish ('... ouqbnovtw ryuq uyatsq jqntb ...', 13 texts); bare ryu (113 texts) stands before its epithet in the F4 invocation and in non-initial phrases ('ryu ryu kfrqfqw', 'ryu hqfgt bt', 'htaqbt ryuby'). When an epithet follows, the ending moves to each word of the phrase: 'ryu rtbmsqmgtfq uyaq rtbaaq', 'ryu gtbmsqegtfq uyaq gtbaaq'. uyat + sq is written apart ('uyat sq') in 71 texts and joined ('uyatsq') in 87. Caveat: xuyaq also occurs outside the invocation (T0016 family), so -q may partly be lexical.

morphemes.function: Address or dative-like ending on titles in the royal texts ('O king' or 'for the king'), probably the same ending as the invocation -sq.
morphemes.evidence: Kharamadoye has a chain of parallel clauses where the title that opens each clause comes back with -(m)sq after fr: 'gyat kehbtwt fr gyatsq', 'bv keybt wt fr bvmsq', 'ga xaqbtmfqwt fr gamsq', 'wyo vfoq fqwt fr wyomsq', 'vahvt knjyntfqwt fr vahvmsq'. Hamadab lists 'gyatmsq ... hgamsq htwbymsq'. The invocation epithet rtbmsq has the same ending.

morphemes.function: Ending of personal names and of the place or office specifier after a title (an onomastic or 'of PLACE' ending).
morphemes.evidence: 6 of the 17 unmasked fillers of the name slot end in st (hbt yst, x nst, u gy st, xhm ofst, gy tst, fq st), as do names nominated in long texts (bktst, kfqst, htfst, eqst, njqgyatst) and parents' names (xbqstbktst btaqntfyrq, xktmst btjvtfyrq, njqgyayst btjvtfyrq, xnjqst btjvtfyrq). After titles it fills the specifier slot: rykeqbp oabyst (compare rykeqbp unfbt), kftntsyw batst / xbyst / jynyst / gygyst / bnatst / stbtnst, btktsfp gyst, nrb fgyst. Bare / -st pairs: xby / xbyst, bat / batst, kftnt / kftntst, kfq / kfqst, stbtn / stbtnst, gy / gyst. 68 word types end in -st.

morphemes.function: Demonstrative / deictic 'this (one)' pointing at the person named; with the copula, gy-rq / gt-rq 'this is'.
morphemes.evidence: It brackets the name in the nomination of every long formula ('gy NAME gyrq', gyrq in 135 texts; 'gt hbt yst gtrq', gtrq in 71) and in short frames ('gy vovm X gy htaqbt ryuby', 'gy vovt fp X gy'). It follows a name as an optional apposition, 'NAME gy' (about 100 times, at any NAME position). gy and gt alternate as the vowel letters y and t do in -fy / -ft.

morphemes.function: Verbal prefix of the offering-wish verbs, most likely a wish (optative / jussive) mood marker; h- and o- are variants used in different text families.
morphemes.evidence: It occurs only on the clause-final word after the offering nouns xby, xb, xbt, never on nouns: h-quqpt-ntw (39 texts), h-uqva-ntw (33), h-uypt-ntw (21), o-uqpt-ov-t-w (13), o-uqva-ov-t-w (13), o-uqbn-ov-t-w (13), 'oq uqptntw' (13), o-uva-ntw (13). The same verb occurs without it (uptntw, 13). Split spellings isolate it: 'hq uy pt ov bt', 'hq uy pt nt w', 'h uy pt o'.

morphemes.function: Verbal suffix between the root and the final ending, perhaps aspect or the plural addressee ('may you two ...'); -ov- is the variant of the F4 family.
morphemes.evidence: They fill the same slot in the same wishes: hquqpt-nt-w vs ouqpt-ov-t-w, huqva-nt-w vs ouqva-ov-t-w. The split spelling 'hq uy pt ov nt w' (T0768) shows both at once, so they are distinct elements.

morphemes.function: Final verbal ending (person / number or mood) alternating -w ~ -bt in otherwise identical wishes; a 2nd-person (plural) imperative or optative addressed to the two deities is the likeliest reading.
morphemes.evidence: hquqptntw (39 texts) vs hquqptntbt and huptntbt (4) / huqptntbt; huqvantw vs huqvantbt; split 'hq uy pt ov bt' vs 'hq uy pt nt w'. The wishes are framed by the address to the two deities (ryuq uyatsq opens the text and, in F4, follows the wishes).

morphemes.function: Not a grammatical morpheme: a word-initial letter (probably an initial-vowel sign) that marks where a written word starts.
morphemes.evidence: 235 word types begin with x; inside a word it appears only where two words are run together (stbkjtfyrqxbtgq, gyrqxby, ubtxgtotbyrq, huqptntbtxb). The same element has x when written alone and none when attached: 'stbkjt xgtotbyrq' (99) vs stbkjtgtotbyrq (4); 'st b kjt xgt otw fy' vs 'st b kjt gt otw fy'; xuyat beside uyat. This makes x a reliable cue for cutting run-together words.

morphemes.function: Derivational prefix forming the general kin term stbkjt ('relative') from kjt (narrower relation, perhaps 'descendant / child').
morphemes.evidence: kjt occurs on its own (16 texts) and with other endings (kjt-byrq in 86 texts, kjtw, kjtwf, 'kjt fr'), while stbkjt is the commonest word (1,403 tokens of stbkjtfyrq in 236 texts). Split spellings mark a boundary before kjt: 'stb kjt fy rq' (7) and 'st b kjt gt otw fy' (7).

morphemes.function: Postposed qualifier (adjective-like, e.g. 'great / chief') after a title or noun; it can itself be determined and predicated.
morphemes.evidence: It follows titles and nouns: 'btkts fp' (9) / btktsfp (74 tokens), bktsfp (33), bbmfp (13), xhybtfp, 'RNAME gyatfp', ujabtfp, 'gy vovt fp X gy' (21). It takes the determiner and copula like a noun: 'xotwst njqbt fpfyrq' (33), fpfto (4), 'btktsnjq fp joatbtfyrq'.

morphemes.function: List-closing quantifier or conjunction ('all of these / together') before a summarising, usually plural, predicate.
morphemes.evidence: 58 tokens. It stands right before plural-possessor predicates after lists: '... kftntsyw bnatst ntfr stbkjtotbyrq' (21), '... katogy gyaybto ntfr stbkjt xgtotbyrq' (13), 'kftntsyw h kftntsyw h ntfr st b kjt otw fy', and after counted items: '... btntbq 59 stj bfb 16 ntfr sqnqjoqbtfyrq' (13), 'w 10 ntfr xvqjt'.

morphemes.function: Derivational suffix on titles and nouns; meaning unclear (perhaps an adjectival or collective form).
morphemes.evidence: Pairs vahv / vahvm (8 / 69 texts), gyat / gyatm (118 / 9), vovt / vovtm (21 / 9), bv / bvm, xat / xatm. It stands before the address ending -sq (vahvmsq, gyatmsq, bvmsq, rtbmsq).

word_classes.note: The commonest word (1,403 tokens of stbkjtfyrq). Head of the DESCRIPTION slot 'TITLE NAME stbkjtfyrq' = '(the deceased) is a relative of TITLE NAME'; built from kjt with stb-.

FILIATION slot, right after the nomination; bjvt fills the same slot with the same ending (45 texts). Probably the mother ('born of'): three parent names before it contain njq (njqgyayst, xnjqst, njqotjtrtbtf), none before btaqnt.
The other FILIATION term (195 texts), probably the father: its holder twice carries an office title (xhybt xoast, htwby fpst).
Second relation type in F1, 'gyat wkft NAME kjtbyrq' ('is a kjt [descendant?] of the court official NAME'); root of stbkjt.
Third relation term, the usual predicate of the short frames ('vahvm hvaw bt X njqbt fy rq').
Further relation predicates in F2 ('haue htftnfqx NAME wkfyrq', 'NAME ubtfyrq', 'btktsnjq fp joatbtfyrq'); wk also in the court title gyat wk-ft.

word_classes.class: predicate noun (status or kin term) used as an apposition
word_classes.note: Follows any NAME as an optional apposition ('NAME kyntfyrq', 94 times) and forms a one-word label ('X kyntfyrq').
Optional apposition after a name, 'NAME ktbt f' (92), with the determiner written apart; also inside names (otnt ktbt, bgy ktbt f).
Fills the deceased slot (gy NAME gyrq), the parent slots (before btjvt / btaqnt) and the holder slots (after a title, before stbkjtfyrq). Never takes the determiner -f-.

word_classes.form: hbt yst, xhm ofst, kd rqba, kfqba qjt, kfq btrte, bmfvt xaya, kwvbt bayoqb, urt qoa, v fyen, jbtgyv gy, otnt ktbt, njq gtobw, x nst, u gy st, gy tst, fq st, bgy ktbt f

word_classes.note: OFFERING WISH slot. Each selects its own verb root: xby + -pt- (111 clauses), xb + -va- (68), xbt + -bn- (14).
Follows the offering noun (xby kpt, xb kvt), so modifiers follow their head; also predicated in 'X kptrqba'.

Follow the counted noun: eoafqw 1, otfbyat 1, htee 5, jy 6, rt w 12, btntbq 59, bfb 16, xoa 32 njq 135.

word_classes.form: rq, fy, f (written as separate words)
word_classes.note: rq is the copula (313 free tokens), fy and f the determiner (fy 214, f 426); their free spelling is the main evidence that -fyrq = -f- + -y- + -rq.
